title: Cubic & reciprocal graphs
examples: What is the difference between a cubic and a reciprocal graph?
How do I find the asymptotes for a function like one over x?
Can you show me a graph that looks like a cubic function?

explain.say: Today we look at two types of graphs. We will study cubic and reciprocal shapes. These graphs have very distinct features you should know.
A cubic graph generally has an 'S' shape. It goes up, then down, and then up again. This shape is characteristic of polynomial functions.
The graph of one over x is a reciprocal function. It has two separate curves in opposite quadrants. It never touches the axes.
For the reciprocal graph, we look for asymptotes. These are lines the graph approaches but never crosses. The vertical asymptote is x equals zero.
Another important asymptote for one over x is the horizontal one. This line is y equals zero. The graph gets closer and closer to it.

faq.a: A cubic graph is generally described by a polynomial with the highest power of x being three. It has that characteristic 'S' shape.
asks: What is the shape of a cubic function?
How do I tell if a graph is cubic?

faq.a: An asymptote is a line that the graph gets infinitely close to but never actually touches. Think of it as a boundary line.
asks: What does it mean for a graph to approach a line?

faq.q: Why does one over x have asymptotes at x equals zero and y equals zero?
faq.a: When x is zero, you cannot divide by it, so the graph shoots up or down near that line. When y is zero, the graph gets very close to the x-axis.
asks: Why can't the graph cross the y-axis?
What happens when x gets very small?

faq.q: Is the cubic graph always increasing?
faq.a: No, the cubic graph changes direction. It goes up, then it turns and goes down, before turning up again.
asks: Does the cubic graph always go up?
Can a cubic graph have a maximum point?

faq.q: Can a graph have more than one asymptote?
faq.a: Yes, the reciprocal function one over x has two asymptotes. One is vertical and one is horizontal.
asks: How many asymptotes can a rational function have?
Do I need to find both types of asymptotes?

facts: A cubic function has a degree of three in its polynomial equation.
The graph of one over x has a vertical asymptote at x equals zero.
The graph of one over x has a horizontal asymptote at y equals zero.
The general shape of a cubic graph resembles the letter 'S'.

quiz.say: Which graph has a vertical asymptote at x equals zero and a horizontal asymptote at y equals zero?
quiz.show: Graph with asymptotes at x=0, y=0

options.show: A straight line through the origin
options.say: A straight line through the origin

options.show: The graph of y equals one over x
options.say: The graph of y equals one over x

quiz.why: The function one over x is the classic example that has both these specific asymptotes.

wrong.0: A straight line does not have asymptotes like this function does.
wrong.1: A parabola has a minimum point, not asymptotes at zero.
wrong.2: A cubic graph changes direction but does not have these specific asymptotes.

quiz.say: If a graph has the general 'S' shape, what type of function is it likely to be?
quiz.why: The 'S' shape is the defining visual characteristic of a cubic polynomial graph.

wrong.0: A quadratic function forms a U-shape or an inverted U-shape.
wrong.1: A linear function is always a perfectly straight line.
wrong.2: A reciprocal function has two separate branches, not a continuous 'S' shape.

quiz.say: Which graph is best described by having two separate branches that approach the axes?

options.show: The graph of y equals one over x
options.say: The graph of y equals one over x

quiz.why: The reciprocal function naturally splits into two parts, one in the first quadrant and one in the third.

wrong.1: A cubic graph is continuous and does not separate into two distinct pieces.
wrong.2: A parabola is a single, continuous curve shape.
wrong.3: This line passes through the origin and is not separated by asymptotes.
